content: {"rule": "K-S2", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The text issues an UNDERDETERMINED verdict with stated grounds, so the rule constrains what may support that verdict.", "verdict": "CLEAN", "quote": "UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4; Mary's phrase 'thy father' is immediately qualified by the child's reference to 'my Father's business.'", "rule_words": "That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side.", "room": "'is immediately qualified' -- read one way, the judge rests the verdict on positive verse-upon-verse content (the child's 'my Father's business' qualifying Mary's 'thy father') and the chain answer cited from [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4; read the other way, it rests on the bare fact that Luke 2:48 does not itself state the link; the first reading fits, since the judge cites what the passage does say, not what a single verse omits.", "why": "The judge's stated ground is the defender's chain answer plus the qualifying content of the companion verse, not the absence of a single-verse statement, so the forbidden ground is never used."}
